chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Zahir, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'We are the guardians of the command of God, and the treasurers of the knowledge of God, and the repositories of the revelation of God.'

key_terms.خَزَنَةُ عِلْمِ اللَّهِ: Treasurers of God's knowledge — the Imams preserve and transmit divine knowledge inaccessible to others
key_terms.عَيْبَةُ وَحْيِ اللَّهِ: Repositories/receptacles of God's revelation — 'ayba' originally means a chest or container; here the Imams are the living vessels of prophetic revelation
key_terms.وُلَاةُ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ: Guardians/masters of God's command — a title of divine vicegerency connecting to Quranic 'uli al-amr' (those in authority, Q. 4:59)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the Imams being guardians of God's command?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) makes a definitive creedal declaration about the unique station of the Imams of Ahl al-Bayt: they are the divinely appointed guardians (wulat) of God's command, the custodians of divine knowledge, and the vessels of divine revelation. This hadith, narrated through a companion of the Imam, establishes the Imams as the exclusive legitimate authorities through whom God's command and knowledge reach the community. The audience of early Shia Muslims would have understood this as a claim to spiritual and religious sovereignty grounded in divine appointment rather than human consensus.
